title: Ops runway: traffic-light roadmap and KPI notes
content:
Purpose: quick-reference sprintboard + traffic-light roadmap to decide go/no-go for feature launches. This is a working doc (notes, thresholds, playbook) intended to be read by product-ops, release leads, SRE, and on-call. Treat as the single source for operational thresholds during the 72h critical window around release.

Context and intent:
- We need a compact signal set that maps to actions (traffic-light) rather than raw numbers. This lives alongside the release checklist but is lighter-weight for on-call and PMs during rollout.
- Keeps decision latency low: each metric has clear owner, threshold for green/yellow/red, and an explicit action.

Traffic-light roadmap (visualize as sprintboard lanes: infra / runtime / UX / metrics):
1) Infra lane (owner: Mateo Alvarez)
   - Green: infra CPU < 60% sustained, GPU utilization within baseline profile, no new OOMs, p95 infra latency < 120ms.
   - Yellow: CPU 60-80% or p95 infra latency 120-220ms, 1-2 minor OOM events with automatic recovery. Action: enable extra burst nodes; notify infra slack @infra-alerts; escalate if sustained > 15m.
   - Red: CPU >80% or sustained OOMs or p95 infra latency > 220ms. Action: pause canary, scale up dedicated pool + fallback model, trigger rollback playbook.

2) Serving/runtime lane (owner: Luca Moreno)
   - Green: model p95 latency < 350ms, token error rate < 0.2%, KV cache hit rate >= 55%.
   - Yellow: model p95 latency 350-650ms OR token error rate 0.2-1%. Action: reduce canary QPS by 50%, enable additional batching guidance, notify runtime channel.
   - Red: latency >650ms or token error rate >1% or KV cache hit < 20%. Action: immediate failover to supported smaller model variant, pause canary, run anomaly capture (trace + payload sample).

3) Product/UX lane (owner: Hannah Cho)
   - Green: end-user task conversion (funnel) stable within +/-5% baseline; no increase in user-facing errors.
   - Yellow: conversion drops 5-12% or user-reported errors increase. Action: reduce rollout cadence (canary -> 5%), deploy client-side messaging, run user-sampling for qualitative checks.
   - Red: conversion drop >12% or new high-severity user errors. Action: pause rollout, surface to exec comms, run rollback or mitigation.

4) Business/KPI lane (owner: Asha Patel)
   - Green: feature-specific KPI (first-week opt-in) on or above target (example: 6% weekly opt-in), feature adoption growth meets forecast.
   - Yellow: KPI 70-90% of target. Action: hold further rollout, run quick funnels and promo work with growth.
   - Red: KPI <70% or negative revenue impact flagged by finance. Action: freeze and open cross-functional review.

Preflight checklist (72h window; checkboxes to tick before canary):
- [ ] All infra runbooks validated and smoke-tested in staging (links to smoke test results).
- [ ] Canary config generated and verified (percentage, routing, rate-limits).
- [ ] Alert rules deployed and verified for p50/p95/p99 on model and infra metrics.
- [ ] Chaos tests: simulated node loss for autoscaler path executed in canary environment.
- [ ] Security and compliance sign-off for data handling (private deployment exceptions noted).
- [ ] Docs updated: user-facing FAQ and internal runbook pinned in release channel.
- [ ] Communication plan drafted for customers and internal teams with timeline and owners.

Go / No-Go decision matrix (simple):
- All lanes green -> proceed to canary -> monitor 6h -> increase per rollout plan.
- Any single lane yellow -> slow-down rollout, apply mitigations, reassess after 30-60 minutes.
- Any single lane red -> immediate pause; execute the mapped red actions; convene incident paraglider (15-min sync).

Canary cadence recommendations (default):
- Step 0: internal smoke (0%) -> Step 1: canary 1% for 1h -> Step 2: canary 5% for 3h -> Step 3: 20% for 6h -> Step 4: 50% for 12h -> Step 5: 100%
- If any lane shows yellow at a step, repeat the step length or revert to previous step after mitigation.

Rollback playbook (short):
- Trigger conditions: red lane OR cumulative user-impact signal > defined threshold.
- Steps: 1) Pause traffic routing to new model variant; 2) Switch traffic to last known good model or region; 3) Clear relevant cache namespaces if corrupted; 4) Notify customers per comms playbook; 5) Open incident with severity and initial timeline; 6) Post-mortem owner assigned within 48h.

Communication plan (internal + external):
- Internal: release-channel pinned message + escalation matrix in #release-ops. Executive brief if red > 30m and impact > 1% DAU.
- External: staging of messaging templates (customer status page, targeted emails). Drafts live in linked Confluence page.

Monitoring dashboard checklist (SRE/monitoring owner must verify):
- Real-time charts for p50/p95/p99, error rate by endpoint, KV cache hit rate, infra CPU/GPU, autoscaler events, rollout % over time.
- Synthetic transactions every 5m across customer regions.
- Automated anomaly detection hook to open a ticket if correlated signals appear across at least 2 lanes.

Quick triage flow (first 15 minutes):
1) Identify lane(s) with red signals and itemize which submetric tripped.
2) Owner posts a 1-3 line hypothesis in release channel.
3) If infra/runtime, collect traces + slow payload sample; if product, get UX capture; if KPI, collect funnel snapshot.
4) Decide: mitigate, scale, or rollback.

Unresolved questions / TODOs (notes to self):
- Decide whether to make KV cache hit threshold dynamic by model family.
- Add a tag-based alert suppression to avoid noisy non-actionable alerts during scheduled scale events.
- Confirm finance-derived dollar-impact threshold for auto-freeze (linked to cost-overrun rule).

Reference notes and quick links:
- Release artifacts: see linked artifacts above.
- Example incident archetype: high-latency spike caused by batching misconfiguration (search JIRA-PI: PRODOPS-412).

Meeting cadence during rollout:
- 0h-6h: 15min standups; 6h-24h: 30min standups; >24h: shift-to-daily until stable. Keep notes in meeting thread (attach sprintboard snapshots).

Post-launch evaluation (within 72h):
- Owner-led readout with: metric deltas vs baseline, user-impact narratives, cost delta, rollout timeline, action items.
- Success criteria: all lanes in green and KPIs within target band for 24h post 100% rollout.

Quick links to artifacts and tickets (copy into incident chat during outages):
- Confluence runbook page: https://confluence.redwood.com/pages/viewpage.action?pageId=15823
- Root Jira epic: PRODOPS-400
- Rollout scripts repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/release-scripts/pull/287

Signoff (fill before final release):
- Product-ops lead: ____________________
- SRE: ____________________
- Runtime: ____________________
- Legal/Compliance (if needed): ____________________

Notes: this is intentionally conversational — live doc for the next three launches. Keep edits small and append comments with initials+date. Last full revision: 2026-03-10 by Asha P.
